data.narrative:
World Labs, a Series A AI & Software company founded by Fei-Fei Li, Ben Mildenhall, Christoph Lassner, and Justin Johnson, has raised $1.23B+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company (Palantir, ticker PLTR), including same-stage and adjacent-stage AI & Software businesses.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline of $1.2B and applying a typical 2.0x Series A step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $2.5B. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Reflection AI ($25.0B Series A), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B Series B), Black Forest Labs ($3.2B Series B), and Field AI ($2.0B Series B)—yields a median valuation of $4.4B, with a range spanning $2.0B to $25.0B.

The two methods triangulate to a valuation range of $2.1B (low) to $5.1B (high), with a median implied value of $3.4B. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around the appropriate multiple for early-stage frontier AI companies, where recent comps show significant variance depending on traction, team pedigree, and capital efficiency. The outlier valuation of Reflection AI at $25.0B introduces upside asymmetry; conversely, stage-progression conservatism anchors the downside.
